studies.title: The translational landscape of mTOR signalling steers cancer initiation and metastasis
studies.authors: Hsieh AC; Liu Yi; Edlind MP; Ingolia NT; Janes MR; Sher A; Shi EY; Stumpf CR; Christensen C; Bonham MJ; Wang S; Ren P; Martin M; Jessen K; Feldman ME; Weissman JS; Shokat KM; Rommel C; Ruggero D

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed WHY mTOR-driven translation matters for cancer: in prostate cancer, oncogenic mTOR selectively translates a specific set of pro-invasion mRNAs that drive metastasis. An ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (INK128) reversed that signature - an early preclinical rationale from mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition augments antitumor immune effector response by reprogramming the TP53-mutant, immune-cold HNSCC tumor microenvironment
studies.authors: Nath P; Khandelwal A; Li C; Moore-Medlin T; Vasudevan SS; Alvarez VA; Franco OE; Gutkind JS; Nathan CO

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Syngeneic mouse models of TP53-mutant HNSCC
studies.finding: In syngeneic TP53-mutant HNSCC mouse models, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus reprogrammed the immune-cold tumor microenvironment: it increased CD8+ T cell and dendritic cell infiltration, reduced Tregs and HIF-1α/VEGFA-driven MDSC recruitment, boosted TNF-α/CXCL10 chemokine signaling, and reduced PD-1/PD-L1 expression — restoring T-cell cytotoxic competence and suppressing tumor growth.

studies.title: mTORC1 stimulates cell growth through SAM synthesis and m6A mRNA-dependent control of protein synthesis
studies.authors: Villa E; Sahu U; O'Hara BP; Ali ES; Helmin KA; Asara JM; Gao P; Singer BD; Ben-Sahra I

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: SAMTOR (GU2017) showed the cell can sense S-adenosylmethionine and report it to mTORC1. This study runs the arrow the other way: mTORC1 controls how much SAM the cell makes. Downstream of mTORC1, c-MYC binds intron 1 of MAT2A and raises expression of the enzyme that produces SAM, the cell's main methyl donor; mTORC1 separately increases the protein level of WTAP, the regulatory subunit of the m6A RNA methyltransferase complex. Together these raise m6A methylation of mRNA, which primes the translation machinery for growth. Blocking MAT2A lowers SAM, m6A, protein synthesis rate and tumor growth.

studies.title: Synergistic role of TFEB/TFE3 and mTORC1 in kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis
studies.authors: Ferniani M; Sambri I; Huynh T; Pennella R; Tufano G; Herz NJ; Rossi B; Iannaccone A; Trepiccione F; Calcagnì A; Ballabio A

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Kidney-specific conditional knockout mice: Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO (models of Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex)
studies.finding: Using kidney-specific mouse models that genetically uncouple mTORC1 activity from TFEB/TFE3 activity (Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO), the authors show mTORC1 hyperactivation -- not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone -- is the primary driver of kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis in Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex models. Constitutive TFEB/TFE3 activity further accelerates disease on top of mTORC1-driven pathology.

studies.title: Imaging dynamic mTORC1 pathway activity in vivo reveals marked shifts that support time-specific inhibitor therapy in AML
studies.authors: Oki T; Mercier F; Kato H; Jung Y; McDonald TO; Spencer JA; Mazzola MC; van Gastel N; Lin CP; Michor F; Kitamura T; Scadden DT

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse AML model; intravital imaging of bone marrow with fluorescent probes
studies.finding: Fluorescent probes imaged in the bone marrow of live mice show mTORC1 activity in AML cells falls as the disease progresses but is high at the moment of maximal chemotherapy response, where it is induced rather than selected; inhibiting mTORC1 at that time improved killing of AML cells.

studies.title: Firefox, a protein encoded by circular PVT1, is essential for MYC-driven oncogenesis.
studies.authors: Tiwari A; Paithane U; Tashiro K; Hall B; Friedlein J; Saraswat M; Saulnier O; Barbosa K; Trinh Q; Saha S; Soni A; Nakashima T; Murad R; Maurya S; Chapman OS; James B; Erickson A; Lange JT; Leary R; Varshney J; Konety B; Dehm SM; Kawakami Y; Largaespada DA; Weiss WA; Stein L; Chavez L; Suzuki H; Wu S; Zhao J; Deshpande AJ; Taylor MD; Wechsler-Reya RJ; Bagchi A

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human MYC-amplified cancer cell lines; xenograft mouse models
studies.finding: A micropeptide (Firefox/FFX) encoded by the circular RNA circPVT1 stimulates AKT-mTORC1 signaling and cap-dependent translation to sustain MYC protein abundance and transcriptional output. FFX depletion reduces MYC levels and impairs tumor growth in MYC-amplified xenograft models, identifying an mTORC1-linked vulnerability in MYC-driven cancers.

studies.title: Hypoxia regulates TSC1/2-mTOR signaling and tumor suppression through REDD1-mediated 14-3-3 shuttling
studies.authors: DeYoung MP; Horak P; Sofer A; Sgroi D; Ellisen LW

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: REDD1-/- and TSC2-/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts, human cell lines in 1% O2; xenografts in nude mice; human breast carcinoma samples
studies.finding: Explains how low oxygen turns mTORC1 off. Growth factors keep TSC2 bound to inhibitory 14-3-3 proteins; under hypoxia REDD1 releases TSC2 from 14-3-3, which frees TSC2 to inhibit mTORC1. REDD1-null cells failed to release TSC2 or to switch mTORC1 off in hypoxia, and REDD1 mutants that cannot bind 14-3-3, or TSC2 mutants that cannot bind it, broke the signal. REDD1-null cells grew into far larger tumours in mice, and REDD1 was low in a subset of human breast carcinomas (8 of 27). Boundary: cell lines and mouse xenografts under acute hypoxia (hours); the human data are expression correlations only.

studies.title: Enhanced sensitivity of PTEN-deficient tumors to inhibition of FRAP/mTOR
studies.authors: Neshat MS; Mellinghoff IK; Tran C; Stiles B; Thomas G; Petersen R; Frost P; Gibbons JJ; Wu H; Sawyers CL

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Isogenic PTEN+/+ and PTEN-/- mouse cells and human cancer cell lines, in vitro and as tumours in mice; CCI-779
studies.finding: Tested whether tumour cells that have lost PTEN depend more on mTOR. The rapamycin analogue CCI-779 (temsirolimus) blocked growth of PTEN-null cells and tumours preferentially, and reversed the extra tumour growth caused by constitutively active Akt, placing mTOR downstream of Akt in tumour formation. PTEN loss went with higher S6 kinase activity and S6 phosphorylation. Sensitivity was not explained by how well the drug blocked S6 phosphorylation, since S6 was inhibited in sensitive and resistant lines alike. Boundary: worked from the abstract only (scanned PMC record); mouse and human cell lines and mouse tumour models, not patients.

studies.title: An inhibitor of mTOR reduces neoplasia and normalizes p70/S6 kinase activity in Pten+/- mice
studies.authors: Podsypanina K; Lee RT; Politis C; Hennessy I; Crane A; Puc J; Neshat M; Wang H; Yang L; Gibbons J; Frost P; Dreisbach V; Blenis J; Gaciong Z; Fisher P; Sawyers CL; Hedrick-Ellenson L; Parsons R

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Pten+/- mice treated with a pharmacological mTOR inhibitor
studies.finding: Transformed cells in Pten+/- mice showed raised phosphorylated Akt and active p70 S6 kinase together with faster proliferation. Treating the mice with an mTOR inhibitor reduced neoplastic proliferation, tumour size and S6 kinase activity without changing Akt status. The authors concluded that S6K and possibly other mTOR targets contribute to tumour development downstream of PTEN loss. Boundary: worked from the abstract only (scanned PMC record); mouse model. The abstract does not name the inhibitor.

studies.title: Rapamycin increases lifespan and inhibits spontaneous tumorigenesis in inbred female mice
studies.authors: Anisimov VN; Zabezhinski MA; Popovich IG; Piskunova TS; Semenchenko AV; Tyndyk ML; Yurova MN; Rosenfeld SV; Blagosklonny MV

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Female 129/Sv inbred mice given rapamycin intermittently (2 weeks per month) from 2 months of age for life; survival, body weight, ageing-rate measures and spontaneous tumours
studies.finding: Female 129/Sv inbred mice received rapamycin intermittently, 2 weeks in every month, from 2 months of age for the rest of their lives. Treated mice gained less weight with age, showed a slower estimated rate of ageing, lived longer, with the gain most visible among the last survivors, and developed spontaneous tumours later. 22.9% of rapamycin-treated mice were still alive when the last control mouse died. The paper provided evidence that an intermittent rapamycin schedule can extend lifespan in a normal inbred mouse strain, adding to earlier results in genetically heterogeneous mice. Boundary: Female mice of a single inbred strain (129/Sv) only; drafted from the abstract only, so dose, group sizes and median-lifespan statistics are not given here.

relations.mechanism: Hyperactive mTORC1 reprograms translation toward a specific set of pro-growth and pro-metastasis mRNAs (HSI2012, prostate models) and couples nucleotide synthesis to demand, creating a targetable vulnerability in TSC-deficient cells (VAL2017).
relations.mechanism_beginner: In mouse tumour models and cancer cells where the pathway is already over-active, hyperactive mTORC1 pushes cells to build a specific set of growth- and spread-promoting proteins, and the tumour becomes dependent on that programme.
relations.boundary: Context-dependent: shown in genetically driven mouse tumour models and cancer cell lines with hyperactive mTORC1 (PTEN loss, TSC loss), not as a general property of tumours. OKI2021 (mouse AML) is not cited as support: mTORC1 activity fell as the leukaemia progressed and rose during the chemotherapy response, so it bears on when to inhibit mTORC1, not on mTORC1 driving growth.
relations.note: The arrow means hyperactive mTORC1 promotes tumour growth where the pathway is already unleashed - PTEN-loss and TSC-loss backgrounds. It is not a claim that mTORC1 activity causes tumours generally, and normal mTORC1 signalling is not a tumour driver here.
